newDescription:
In this Year 3 English lesson, pupils learn how adverbs add information to verbs and make sentences more precise and interesting.

This lesson includes:
✔ Revisiting verbs and identifying the action in a sentence
✔ Understanding that adverbs can tell us how, when, where or why something happens
✔ Identifying adverbs such as quickly, gently and always
✔ Recognising that many adverbs end in -ly, while some do not
✔ Adding suitable adverbs to sentences
✔ Finding adverbs in different positions within a sentence
✔ Using adverbs to add detail and create clearer mental pictures
✔ Experimenting with adverb position and noticing how word order can affect meaning
✔ Using adverbs in speech to show how somebody has spoken

Pupils begin by revisiting verbs before exploring how adverbs add extra information to an action. Through mime, sentence work and short independent activities, they identify adverbs and explain what each one tells the reader.

The lesson then develops adverb use in writing. Pupils create their own sentences from a photograph, move adverbs to different positions and consider how this changes the sound or meaning of a sentence.

The final activity focuses on speech, where pupils choose suitable adverbs to describe how different characters speak.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify adverbs, explain the information they add, and use them effectively in their own sentences.
